paragraphs.title: The Command Concerning the Prophet and the Destruction of Family and Society

answers: Take a wife or have sons and daughters
Leave the city
Speak to the people
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Jeremiah not to take a wife or have children in that place.
easy.q: What was Jeremiah commanded not to do?

answers: Only kings
Sons, daughters, mothers, and fathers
Only priests
easy.explanation: The passage mentions children, their mothers, and their fathers.
easy.q: Who is specifically included in the judgment?

answers: By grievous deaths, the sword, and famine
By old age alone
By drowning and fire
easy.explanation: They would die of grievous deaths and be consumed by the sword and famine.

answers: There were no houses available
The land faced destruction and death
The people opposed marriage
medium.explanation: The command served as a sign of the coming disaster upon families and the land.
medium.q: Why was Jeremiah forbidden to establish a family there?

answers: They would receive honorable burial
They would be carried to another land
They would be as dung and eaten by birds and beasts
medium.explanation: Their bodies would not be buried and would become food for birds and beasts.
medium.q: What would happen to the bodies of the dead?

answers: Deaths caused by disease and calamity
Deaths only in battle
Deaths in old age
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to terrible deaths connected with the coming judgment.
medium.q: What does the phrase “grievous deaths” describe?

answers: His life would become a sign of the society’s distress
He would become a king
He would leave his prophetic office
challenge.explanation: His lack of a family reflected the destruction coming upon families in the land.
challenge.q: What does Jeremiah’s personal command signify?

answers: The dead would be buried with their fathers
There would be neither burial nor mourning
The dead would receive new names
challenge.explanation: The passage stresses both the absence of burial and the absence of lamentation.
challenge.q: Which detail especially emphasizes the greatness of the disaster?

answers: They explain why he should not raise a family there
They describe a family celebration
They explain why Jeremiah should marry
challenge.explanation: These disasters would devastate families and children in the land.
challenge.q: How do the sword, famine, and grievous deaths relate to Jeremiah’s command?

paragraphs.title: The End of Mourning and Celebration

answers: The house of mourning and the house of feasting
The king’s house only
The schoolhouse only
easy.explanation: He was told not to enter the house of mourning or the house of feasting.
easy.q: Which houses was Jeremiah forbidden to enter?

answers: Peace, lovingkindness, and mercies
Their clothing and houses
Rain and harvest
easy.explanation: The Lord said He had taken away His peace, lovingkindness, and mercies.
easy.q: What had the Lord taken away from the people?

answers: Only the voices of war
The voice of mirth, gladness, the bridegroom, and the bride
Only the voices of animals
easy.explanation: The Lord would cause all these voices of joy and celebration to cease.
easy.q: Which voices would cease from the place?

answers: They would not be buried or lamented
They would receive a comfort feast
They would be taken to houses of feasting
medium.explanation: No one would bury or mourn them, nor offer the usual consolation.
medium.q: What would happen to the dead according to verses 6–7?

answers: A place for a meal and celebration
A burial cave
A place of prayer
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a house where people gathered to eat and drink.
medium.q: What is a house of feasting in this context?

answers: The joy and feasting were about to cease
He had no food
He had to attend a funeral
medium.explanation: The command pointed to the coming removal of celebration from the land.
medium.q: Why was Jeremiah forbidden to sit in the house of feasting?

answers: Both show that ordinary social life would be broken
Only celebration would end
Mourning would be replaced by feasting
challenge.explanation: The passage describes the destruction of both mourning customs and joyful gatherings.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the end of mourning and the end of celebration?

answers: Attend a feast, comfort mourners, then marry
Do not enter the mourning house, mourn with them, or enter the feasting house
Marry, have children, and leave the land
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah was to avoid both mourning ceremonies and feasting gatherings.
challenge.q: Which sequence best summarizes the Lord’s commands to Jeremiah?

answers: Their wedding would be unusually large
Their voices represent the end of family and public celebration
They would lead the people
challenge.explanation: Their voices are clear examples of the joy that would be silenced.
challenge.q: Why are the bridegroom and bride mentioned?

paragraphs.title: The People’s Sins and the Cause of Exile

answers: Why the Lord had pronounced this evil and what their sin was
When the temple would be rebuilt
Who the next king would be
easy.explanation: They would ask why this great evil had come upon them and what sin they had committed.
easy.q: What would the people ask Jeremiah?

answers: Forsaken the Lord and served other gods
Built new cities
Kept the Lord’s law perfectly
easy.explanation: Their fathers forsook the Lord, followed other gods, and worshipped them.

answers: Into the same land only
Into a land unknown to them and their fathers
Into the temple
easy.explanation: They would be cast into a land that neither they nor their fathers knew.
easy.q: Where would the Lord cast the people?

answers: It had done less evil
It had done worse and followed the imagination of its evil heart
It had kept the law better
medium.explanation: The people had done worse than their fathers and followed their evil hearts.
medium.q: How had the present generation sinned compared with its fathers?

answers: Stubbornly following one’s own sinful desires
Having a joyful heart
Possessing great wisdom
medium.explanation: The phrase describes following one’s own stubborn and sinful desires instead of obeying God.
medium.q: What does “the imagination of his evil heart” mean?

answers: Serve other gods day and night
Return immediately to Judah
Serve no one
medium.explanation: They would serve other gods day and night in the land of exile.
medium.q: What would the people do in the foreign land?

answers: It first recalls the fathers’ sins and then the present generation’s worse sins
It denies that the people sinned
It mentions only punishment and no sin
challenge.explanation: The answer compares the fathers’ apostasy with the greater evil of the present generation.
challenge.q: How is the prophet’s answer to the people structured?

answers: Disobedience is presented as the reason for being cast into a foreign land
Disobedience guarantees safety in the land
There is no relationship
challenge.explanation: The people would be exiled because they refused to hearken to the Lord.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between refusing to hearken to the Lord and exile?

answers: They would serve other gods day and night
They would receive complete rest
They would remain in their own houses
challenge.explanation: The phrase “day and night” shows the continual nature of their service to other gods.
challenge.q: Which detail emphasizes the severity of the exile?

paragraphs.title: The Consolation of a Redemption Greater Than the Exodus

answers: Bring them again into their own land
Leave them scattered forever
End their identity as a people
easy.explanation: The Lord promised to bring Israel again into the land given to their fathers.
easy.q: What would the Lord do for Israel in the future?

answers: From Egypt only
From the land of the north and all the lands where they had been driven
From the mountains only
easy.explanation: He would bring them from the north and from all the lands of their dispersion.
easy.q: From where would the Lord bring them?

answers: The bringing up of Israel from Egypt
The building of houses
The birth of children
easy.explanation: People would no longer speak only of the Lord who brought Israel out of Egypt.
easy.q: Which former event would no longer be the central oath?

answers: The Lord’s bringing Israel from the north and all the lands
The building of coastal cities
The destruction of families
medium.explanation: The future deliverance would be remembered as the bringing of Israel from all the scattered lands.
medium.q: What would replace the former reference to the Exodus?

answers: After scattering, the Lord would restore the people to their land
The exile would last forever
Israel would have no homeland
medium.explanation: The promise of restoration follows the warning of exile.
medium.q: Why is this promise a consolation in the middle of the prophecy of exile?

answers: The places to which the Lord had scattered or expelled them
The places to which He had brought them near
Places where He had hidden them
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the lands into which Israel had been driven.
medium.q: What does “whither he had driven them” mean?

answers: The future redemption would be so great that it would become the better-known deliverance
The Exodus would be erased from history
The future redemption would be smaller
challenge.explanation: The future return from many lands would be remembered as an especially great act of deliverance.
challenge.q: What does the comparison with the Exodus mean?

answers: Exile, gathering from the nations, and return to the land
Marriage, war, and city building
Feasting, mourning, and the Exodus
challenge.explanation: The verses move from the lands of dispersion to the promised return to Israel’s land.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in these verses?

answers: The Lord is the One who brings Israel out and brings them back
Israel returns by its own strength
The redemption occurs without the Lord
challenge.explanation: In both cases, the Lord is presented as the Redeemer who brings Israel out.
challenge.q: What remains constant in both the former and future deliverance?

paragraphs.title: Exile, the Seen Sin, and Punishment

answers: Fishers and hunters
Shepherds and farmers
Sailors and merchants
easy.explanation: The Lord would send many fishers and then many hunters to capture them.
easy.q: What images describe the capture of the people?

answers: Yes, in caves only
No, because His eyes are upon all their ways
Yes, if they left the land
easy.explanation: Their ways and iniquity were not hidden from the Lord’s eyes.
easy.q: Could the sinners hide from the Lord’s sight?

answers: They had defiled the land with detestable and abominable things
They had built houses
They had kept the law
easy.explanation: They had defiled the Lord’s land and filled His inheritance with abominations.
easy.q: Why would the people be punished?

answers: They portray a thorough capture from which escape would be difficult
They describe ordinary commerce
They teach how to fish
medium.explanation: The two images emphasize that the people would be sought out and captured everywhere.
medium.q: Why are both fishers and hunters mentioned?

answers: Their sin was not hidden from the Lord
Their sin was forgiven
Their sin became righteousness
medium.explanation: The Lord declares that their iniquity was fully visible to Him.
medium.q: What does “their iniquity hid from mine eyes” mean?

answers: On every mountain, hill, and in the holes of the rocks
Only inside city houses
Only in open fields
medium.explanation: The search would include mountains, hills, and rocky hiding places.

answers: The punishment responds to sins fully known to the Lord
The punishment is random
Seeing their ways cancels the punishment
challenge.explanation: Because the Lord sees their ways and iniquity, He can justly recompense their sin.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the Lord seeing all their ways and their punishment?

answers: The hunters would search the holes of the rocks
The fishers would remain only at sea
The people would stay indoors
challenge.explanation: Even natural places of concealment would be searched.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that fugitives would find no secure hiding place?

answers: They had filled the Lord’s inheritance with detestable and abominable things
They were described as minor mistakes
They had no connection with the land
challenge.explanation: The language shows that their abominations had defiled and filled the land.
challenge.q: How severe are the people’s sins portrayed to be?

paragraphs.title: Recognition of God and the Futility of Idols

answers: As his strength, fortress, and refuge
As the king of the enemy
As merely a guide
easy.explanation: Jeremiah calls the Lord his strength, fortress, and refuge.
easy.q: How does Jeremiah describe the Lord?

answers: They are true and profitable
They are lies, vanity, and things with no profit
They are stronger than the Lord
easy.explanation: The Gentiles would recognize that their inherited idols were false and useless.
easy.q: What would the Gentiles say about the gods inherited from their fathers?

answers: His hand and His might
Only the names of kings
The ways of trade
easy.explanation: The Lord promised to make His hand and His might known.
easy.q: What would the Lord make known to the nations?

answers: The Gentiles
Only the priests
Only Jeremiah’s children
medium.explanation: The verse says that the Gentiles would come to Him from the ends of the earth.
medium.q: Who would come to the Lord from the ends of the earth?

answers: A place of protection in trouble
A judgment against Jeremiah
A source of food
medium.explanation: A refuge is a place of safety and protection during distress.
medium.q: What does “my refuge in the day of affliction” mean?

answers: Human-made objects cannot truly become gods
Every man is a god
Idols are more useful than the Lord
medium.explanation: The rhetorical question exposes the foolishness of treating human creations as gods.
medium.q: What does the question “Shall a man make gods unto himself?” imply?

answers: They will turn from idols to acknowledge the Lord
They will worship more idols
They will reject all spiritual knowledge
challenge.explanation: They will recognize the vanity of idols and come to the Lord.
challenge.q: What change is expected among the Gentiles?

answers: The Lord’s revealed hand and might will show that idols have no profit
The idols will overcome the Lord
There is no connection
challenge.explanation: God’s power will expose the emptiness and uselessness of idols.
challenge.q: How do the closing verses relate God’s power to the idols?

answers: Israel and the Gentiles
Jeremiah alone
The idol worshippers alone
challenge.explanation: The promise of recognition extends to the nations as well as God’s people.
challenge.q: Who is expected to know the Lord’s name at the conclusion?
